decisive_items: bilateral facial nerve enhancement compatible with bilateral facial neuritis
bilateral lower motor neuron facial muscle weakness
without evidence of intracranial or leptomeningeal malignancy
response.rationale: MRI demonstrates bilateral facial nerve enhancement, directly confirming facial neuritis as the specific cause of the bilateral lower motor neuron facial weakness. The other options are either broader descriptions or relate to prior, separate clinical issues.

rejected.why: Too broad; it describes the lower motor neuron pattern of weakness but not the specific inflammatory facial nerve etiology shown on MRI.
Prior stable grade 1 chemotherapy-related peripheral neuropathy does not explain the new bilateral facial nerve enhancement and facial weakness.
Capillary leak syndrome explains previous edema but not the bilateral facial neuritis or lower motor neuron facial weakness.
